title: Longspan retrieval degradation profiles and prompt cases
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures an exploratory suite of experiments aimed at characterizing degradation modes when using retrieval-augmented prompts across long context targets (8k, 32k, 128k). The emphasis is on emergent truncation artifacts, attention allocation drift, and retrieval chain fragility when KV cache / prefix prefetching and windowed decoding are active. Goal is to produce a compact set of prompt cases and regression signals we can run in CI for onboarding new model variants.

Scope and constraints:
- Models: internal open-weight family variants (v1.2, v1.3-quant, v2.0). Some tests include a 4-bit quantized build to mimic customer deployments.
- Inference modes: streaming and non-streaming; KV cache enabled/disabled; prefix prefetch window sizes: 0 (none), 64, 512 tokens.
- Workloads: three longdoc modes: 8k (typical long note), 32k (book-chapter), 128k (multi-document retrieval stitch).
- Not covered here: multimodal inputs, code-only models.

Test harness and reproducibility:
- Harness: longspan-harness repo (linked above) with a YAML spec describing prompt sets, retrieval traces, and simulated latency spikes.
- Run command (example): 
  python run_eval.py --spec specs/longspan_retrieval_profiles.yaml --model v1.3-quant --kv-cache true --prefetch 512 --output out/v1.3-quant-prefetch512.json
- All random seeds pinned. Retrieval backend mocked with deterministic document ids/embeddings for stable regression.
- Metric extractor: postproc script computes token-level perplexity (on golden completion), first-token divergence, prefix-attention-entropy, and retrieval-hit-rate.

Dataset and prompt set design (unique aspects):
1) Anchor/Drift series (A1..A12): probe a single anchored question with progressively longer injected irrelevant passages inserted between the prompt and the retrieval snippet. Designed to detect attention sinking into earlier context vs. recent retrieval evidence.
2) Fragmented Retrieval Chain (F1..F8): simulates retrieval producing ordered fragments of an answer spread across multiple documents. Tests whether model reconstructs coherently under window cropping and KV recycling.
3) Truncation Boundary Cases (T1..T6): crafted prompts where the crucial disambiguator token falls exactly at trimming thresholds (8k-1, 8k+1, 32k-1, 32k+1, 128k-1, 128k+1). Useful to capture off-by-one truncation bugs or last-chunk decoding regressions.
4) Posterior Noise Spike (N1..N4): extra repeated tokens appended near the end of context to exercise attention saturation; intended to measure whether attention mass collapses onto noisy suffix.
5) Multi-turn Retrieval Stress (M1..M5): simulated multi-turn chat where retrieval updates each turn. Designed to surface KV-cache misalignment when retrieval result order differs from expected canonical order.

Primary experiment configs (representative):
- Baseline: model v1.2, kv-cache OFF, no prefetch, decode length limited to 256.
- KV/Prefetch: v1.3-quant, kv-cache ON, prefetch=512, decode streaming.
- High-window: v2.0, kv-cache ON, prefetch=8192 (emulate huge prefix), decode non-streaming.
- Short-recycle: v1.3-quant, kv-cache ON with aggressive KV recycle threshold (max_kv_tokens=4096) to force cache eviction mid-answer.

Key observations (summary with examples):
1) Truncation off-by-one regressions: On T3/T4 (32k boundary probes) v1.3-quant dropped the disambiguator token in 18% of runs under streaming mode with prefetch=512. Non-streaming runs showed 0% failure. Hypothesis: streaming chunking logic miscomputes the final chunk length.
2) Attention drift under noisy suffix: For N2, prefix-attention-entropy decreased by 23% and the model started copying noisy suffix tokens into the completion in 12% of trials for v1.2 baseline; stronger in quantized variant. Suggests quantization + attention kernel reorder increases susceptibility to suffix saturation.
3) Fragment assembly failure at 128k: F-series at 128k exhibited higher fragment-mismatch (BLEU-like score drop) when KV recycle threshold < total prefetched tokens. Model would select earlier fragment due to stale KV entries.
4) Retrieval hit rate masking: When retrieval returned closely similar documents (cosine sim > 0.93) for chain fragments, model sometimes ignored higher-quality recent retrievals and used earlier context — more pronounced when prefix prefetch > 1024.

Failure-mode taxonomy (for regression alerts):
- Truncation-on-streaming: any change in streaming chunking that increases missing-disambiguator rate > 5% at boundary test cases.
- KV-eviction-mismatch: when fragment reconstruction score drops by > 10% vs baseline under same model and different KV recycle settings.
- Attention-suffix-collapse: prefix-attention-entropy drop > 15% with increased copy/errors into completion.
- Retrieval-order-flip: multi-turn expected answer alignment > 8% mismatches when retrieval order changed deterministically.

Suggested lightweight regression checks (CI):
- Run T1..T6 at 8k/32k/128k on any new runtime/kernel change in streaming path. Flag if any off-by-one increases beyond baseline.
- Run 3 M-cases (M1,M3,M5) with deterministic retrieval permutations to detect ordering regressions.
- Compare prefix-attention-entropy metric and a small set of human-labeled pass/fail for A-series.

Action items and open questions:
- [A] Add chunk-boundary unit tests for streaming encoder that mock partial last-chunk sizes (owner: Marco, due 2026-03-20).
- [B] Re-run quantized kernel reorder experiments with single-threaded vs multi-threaded builds to isolate source of attention collapse (owner: Lina).
- [C] Build a small determinism harness for retrieval order to ship as part of the longspan-harness.
- Open: is the prefetch heuristic (currently exponential backoff) appropriate for retrieval-heavy multi-document stitching? Consider adding a retrieval-priority override to stop prefetching when fragments are highly dissimilar to the prompt context.

Appendix: quick reproduction notes and config snippets
- Example spec snippet used in harness:
  - prompt_case: T4
    context_size: 32769
    retrieval_trace: ids=[doc_123,doc_124]
    decode: {mode: streaming, max_tokens: 256}
    runtime_flags: {kv_cache: true, prefetch: 512}

- Metrics exported in JSON: {"case":"T4","model":"v1.3-quant","truncation_fail":true,"prefetch":512,"prefix_attention_entropy":1.8,"fragment_score":0.62}

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working draft intended to converge into a smaller set of CI checks. Please comment with any additional boundary cases you've seen in customer incidents.
- Prioritize the streaming chunk off-by-one since several customer-reported incidents roughly match the symptom (last-line missing on very long responses).
